title: We Accidentally Started a Farm and Make $10K/Week

stated_problem.quote: We didn't intend to start a farm, but the more we learned about the food in the grocery store, we just didn't feel comfortable feeding that to our family.
stated_problem.speaker: Vicki

idea.name: Seven Oaks direct-to-consumer beef farm
idea.one_liner: A family farm raises beef, including Wagyu, and sells cuts directly to families through its farm store, with on-site visits and events supporting sales.
idea.customer: Families and other consumers who visit the farm store.
idea.offer: Beef by the cut and in shares, including Wagyu; visitors can also meet the animals and learn about the farm.
idea.revenue_model: Direct retail beef sales, with ticketed events and food sales also contributing to the farm business.

key_quotes.quote: We have five kids here that we raised with us on the farm and we raised beef cows.
So we have chosen to focus on selling direct to consumers.
So I would say social media is our number one.
Everything's individually packaged, vacuum-sealed, frozen, and it comes back, just like this.

claims.claim: The opening says the farm makes $10,000 a week.
claims.quote: Out of this couple built a $10,000 a week farm with zero experience.

claims.claim: The farm started with four cows and later had over 200.
claims.quote: We started with just four cows and now we have over 200.

claims.claim: A monthly farm cost is stated, but the amount is garbled in the transcript.
claims.quote: Our monthly fee cost is about $%$%$%$%$%$%$% dollars.

claims.claim: The host says the cattle can be worth about $10,000 each.
claims.quote: And these guys, they can be worth about $10,000.

claims.claim: The farm covers about 70 acres.
claims.quote: So our farm is about 70 acres.

claims.claim: They have around 30 Wagyu cattle.
claims.quote: I would say we probably have around 30 of them.

claims.claim: The host asks whether a Wagyu cow is worth about $10,000 to $12,000; the transcript does not show a direct confirmation of that figure.
claims.quote: I mean, about 10 to 12 K a cow?

claims.claim: Feed costs are about $22,000 to $25,000 a month.
claims.quote: And we spend probably about $22,000 to $25,000 a month.

claims.claim: They estimate generic feed could cut the feed cost by at least half.
claims.quote: It would probably be at least half cost difference.

claims.claim: Cows are typically processed before age two.
claims.quote: So typically all the cows are processed before they're the age of two.

claims.claim: The farm had operated for about nine and a half years, and the store had opened about a year and a half earlier.
claims.quote: So we have had the farm about nine and a half years now and then we just built this farm store about a year and a half ago.

claims.claim: The farm store build cost between $60,000 and $80,000.
claims.quote: It was between $60 to $80,000, but I can buy that from Danny.

claims.claim: An average cow yields about 450 pounds of beef.
claims.quote: So it varies by cow, but I would say an average is around 450 pounds.

claims.claim: The herd is around 200 to 250 cows.
claims.quote: Now we have all together, probably, around 200, 250 cows.

claims.claim: The host says ten or twenty cattle on one acre would quickly damage the land.
claims.quote: Yeah, because you can't put ten, twenty counts on one acre, right? They'll destroy that really quickly.

claims.claim: They estimate a current profit margin of about 10%.
claims.quote: So now, we're probably at about a 10% profit margin.

claims.claim: They hope to reach a 21% profit margin.
claims.quote: So we are hoping to get up to about a 21% margin once you've gotten it.

claims.claim: A speaker estimates the current margin at 5% to 10%.
claims.quote: You know, 5 to 10% is just my well guess.

claims.claim: The host refers to gross revenue of roughly $40,000.
claims.quote: So we mentioned 40K and gross revenue, roughly.

claims.claim: A guest gives an average gross revenue figure of 40,000, but the period is unclear in the transcript.
claims.quote: Yeah, I'm going to be 40 grand average.

claims.claim: A later expense breakdown puts feed at roughly 20,000, with no period stated in that line.
claims.quote: And that is going to be roughly 20,000.

claims.claim: The farm has five or six people working there.
claims.quote: Yeah, it's, you know, five or six.

claims.claim: Labor costs are roughly 8,000; the period is not stated in the answer.
claims.quote: For now, what are we spending on labor? We're roughly 8,000.

claims.claim: Veterinary care costs about 1,500 monthly.
claims.quote: Probably a monthly, maybe 1,500.

claims.claim: They target about 3,000 a month for fences or barns.
claims.quote: I hit a target of about 3,000 a month to build fences or barns.

claims.claim: The host calculates about $3,500 left after $40,000 in revenue.
claims.quote: And so that really leaves us after $40,000 in revenue with $3,500.

claims.claim: A guest confirms a remaining amount of about $4,000 to $4,500.
claims.quote: Yep. Me too. $4,000 to $4,500.

claims.claim: They estimate total investment in the farm at $1 million to $1.5 million.
claims.quote: How much do you think you would have already invested into seven Oaks farm? Million, million and a half.

claims.claim: They later say they are aiming for a 20% profit margin.
claims.quote: But these are around 5 to 10%. Right? We're shooting for 20.

acquisition_channels.details: Family members, friends and customers referred others to the farm.
Customers visited the farm and store, met the animals and bought meat.
They post about the farm experience on Instagram and Facebook and describe their marketing as mostly organic content.

ideas.delivery: The family raises cattle on the farm and sends them to a family-owned processor. Packaged, vacuum-sealed, frozen meat returns to the farm store for customers to buy.

prices: $10,000 to $12,000 per Wagyu cow, posed by the host

ideas.other_uk_rules: If operated in the UK, food-business registration, food hygiene, meat traceability and livestock identification and welfare requirements would be relevant.

idea.name: Tree pruning and care service
idea.one_liner: Danny describes pruning and caring for trees as his background work; the transcript does not state the customers or business model.

key_quotes.quote: We pruned trees to care of them.

ideas.delivery: Physical tree work; the transcript gives no delivery or staffing details.
ideas.other_uk_rules: If operated in the UK, check consent requirements for protected trees and relevant workplace safety requirements.

idea.name: Farm visits and ticketed events
idea.one_liner: The farm hosts family visits and events such as cooking classes, line dancing and farm-to-table dinners, using them to sell tickets, build awareness and support beef sales.
idea.customer: Families, farm visitors and event attendees.
idea.offer: On-site farm experiences, including free animal visits and selected ticketed events.
idea.revenue_model: Tickets for some events; other visits are free, with food purchases and increased beef sales also supporting the farm.

key_quotes.quote: But if we're doing like a cooking class or the line dancing or a farm to table dinner, we do tickets for those.
Again, it's just to build awareness about the farm, sell more beef and so on and so on.

acquisition_channels.details: They promote events on social media.
Attendees hear about events by word of mouth and bring friends.
Events and visits take place at the farm.

ideas.delivery: The farm hosts visitors on site, with family members and staff arranging animal visits, food and ticketed activities.
ideas.other_uk_rules: If operated in the UK, food hygiene rules apply to food served at events; premises or alcohol licensing may apply depending on the activities.

idea.name: Local farm supplying chicken
idea.one_liner: A local farm supplies chicken to Seven Oaks; the transcript says it uses organic practices but gives no other business details.
idea.customer: Seven Oaks Farms and, potentially, its farm-store customers.
idea.offer: Chicken supplied by a local farm.
idea.revenue_model: Not stated; the transcript only identifies it as a supplier.

key_quotes.quote: We do get chicken from another local farm.
That's also uses organic practices, all of that.

acquisition_channels.details: The farm supplies chicken to Seven Oaks Farms.

ideas.delivery: The local farm raises and supplies chicken; further handling and delivery details are not stated.
ideas.other_uk_rules: If operated in the UK, food hygiene, poultry traceability and livestock welfare requirements would be relevant.

stated_problem.speaker: Vicki

idea.name: Local farms supplying ground beef
idea.one_liner: A couple of nearby farms supply ground beef when Seven Oaks runs out, using practices similar to its own.
idea.customer: Seven Oaks Farms and its farm-store customers.
idea.offer: Ground beef supplied when Seven Oaks' own stock sells out.
idea.revenue_model: The transcript implies sales to Seven Oaks but does not state the terms or prices.

key_quotes.quote: They use similar practices to us.
Would you mind using some ground beef from this farm?

acquisition_channels.details: Seven Oaks has developed relationships with a couple of farms and offers their ground beef when its own supply runs out.

ideas.delivery: Partner farms supply ground beef for the Seven Oaks store when needed.
ideas.other_uk_rules: If operated in the UK, food hygiene and meat traceability requirements would be relevant.

idea.name: Okanember sourdough bread maker
idea.one_liner: A small maker produces sourdough bread shown among the farm store's local goods; customer and sales terms are not stated.
idea.customer: Not stated; the bread is shown at Seven Oaks' farm store.

key_quotes.quote: So you make wonderful bread at Okanember.

ideas.delivery: The maker produces bread; the transcript shows it at the farm store but does not explain the supply arrangement.
ideas.other_uk_rules: If operated in the UK, food-business registration, food hygiene and allergen information requirements would be relevant.

stated_problem.quote: We wanted to try and be able to offer some other products for sale in the farm store beyond what cottage food law allows us to do.
stated_problem.speaker: Vicki

idea.name: Farm food truck and licensed kitchen
idea.one_liner: The farm uses a food truck as a licensed kitchen to prepare meals and other products for sale to visitors and store customers.
idea.customer: Farm visitors and customers seeking prepared meals or other farm products.
idea.offer: Prepared meals and changing menus featuring the farm's meat, plus a licensed kitchen for developing products to sell in the store.
idea.revenue_model: Sales of prepared food and other products; the truck also enhances the farm visit experience.

key_quotes.quote: So by having the food truck, it acts as basically a licensed kitchen.
So people could come out and buy like a prepared meal.

claims.claim: The new food truck cost around $60,000.
claims.quote: I wanted to say it was around 60,000.

acquisition_channels.details: The truck serves visitors on event days and weekends at the farm.
The farm promotes its events on social media.

ideas.delivery: The farm owns the truck; a chef has worked with them, and Vicki and another helper have also run it. It serves food featuring farm meat.

tools: Food truck used as a licensed kitchen

ideas.other_uk_rules: If operated in the UK, food-business registration, food hygiene and allergen requirements would be relevant; additional permissions may apply if trading off site.
